Solution skeleton:
- A(y): β ← {0,1}; if D(yβ) = 1 output β else output 1−β.
- Pr[A(f(U_n)) = b(U_n)] = Pr[D(f(U_n)U₁)=1 ∧ U₁=b(U_n)] + Pr[D(f(U_n)U₁)=0 ∧ 1−U₁=b(U_n)].
- U₁ independent of U_n: = ½·Pr[D(fb)=1] + ½·(1 − Pr[D(fb̄)=1]) = ½ + ½(Pr[D(fb)=1] − Pr[D(fb̄)=1]).
- From D's gap against uniform: |Pr[D(G(U_n))=1] − Pr[D(U_{n+1})=1]| > 1/p(n), and U_{n+1} is fb with prob ½, fb̄ with prob ½, so Pr[D(fb)=1] − Pr[D(fb̄)=1] > 2/p(n) (negating D if the sign is reversed).
- Hence Pr[A(f(U_n)) = b(U_n)] > ½ + 1/p(n), contradicting b hard-core. ∎

Solution skeleton:
- Suppose PPT I inverts f with success δ(n) = Pr_x[I(f(x)) ∈ f⁻¹(f(x))] non-negligible. Because f is 1-1, f⁻¹(f(x)) = {x}, so I(f(x)) = x whenever it succeeds.
- Build predictor A(y) = b(I(y)). Then Pr[A(f(U_n)) = b(U_n)] ≥ Pr[I succeeds] = δ(n).
- If δ(n) > 1/2 + 1/p(n) for some polynomial p, this directly contradicts hard-coreness (advantage over 1/2 must be negligible). So δ(n) is negligible — f is one-way. (One-wayness only requires δ(n) < 1/p(n), which a negligible δ satisfies.) ∎

Solution skeleton:
- x₀ = 3² mod 77 = 9 → LSB 1.
- x₁ = 9² = 81 ≡ 4 (mod 77) → LSB 0.
- x₂ = 4² = 16 → LSB 0.
- x₃ = 16² = 256 ≡ 25 (mod 77) → LSB 1.
- x₄ = 25² = 625 ≡ 9 (mod 77) → LSB 1.
- x₅ = 9² = 81 ≡ 4 (mod 77) → LSB 0.
- First 6 bits: 100110. The state orbit 9 → 4 → 16 → 25 → 9 has period 4, so the LSB sequence is 1,0,0,1 repeated.
- Why x₀ = s²: the BMY/hard-core analysis requires f to be a permutation on the state space. Squaring is a permutation of QR_N but not of Z*_N (the pairs ±x collide). Squaring the seed once places the state inside QR_N, where the map is 1-1. (Also, s² is uniform over QR_N when s is uniform over Z*_N.)
